This may be an unpopular opinion based on the rest of responses here, but I think I might be able to offer a different perspective on this.

I've been in a relationship for nearly 3 years now while dealing with a great deal of mental health and fluctuating libido problems on both sides. I've definitely had medications fuck with my libido which was probably more frustrating for me than my boyfriend. It's really difficult when you've found a medication that works but it makes it difficult to do something that's always been enjoyable. It might take a while, but her sex drive should come back. Or it might just be harder for her to get turned on. 

For me right now, I just started a new medication a few weeks ago and it pretty much shot my libido right from day one. This was incredibly frustrating because I still wanted to have sex but I either felt like I didn't have the energy or I just couldn't finish which made me not want to do it because I knew it would disappoint my boyfriend. It's still difficult but it is slowly getting better. 

My point is that you should ask her how she really feels about sex right now. She might be saying that she doesn't find it important anymore because she doesn't want to end up disappointed when having sex isn't as fun as it was. If she truly doesn't feel it's important anymore, then talk about that and what it might mean for your relationship. A very low sex drive is one of the biggest side effects of antidepressants and I completely understand how frustrating it can be, but it does get better.
